items.followUp: What is the least count of a metre rule, and how is it determined?

rubric.why: This identifies the instrument and its measuring purpose.
rubric.description: Identifies vernier callipers as an instrument for accurate measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a measuring instrument, preferably mentioning measurement of small lengths, diameters or depths.

rubric.why: These are equivalent values for the usual least count of vernier callipers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 0.1 mm or its equivalent, 0.01 cm.

modelAnswer: Vernier callipers are an instrument used to measure small lengths, internal and external diameters, and depths accurately.
Their least count is 0.1 mm (0.01 cm).

items.followUp: Define mass and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: A force is described as a push or a pull.
rubric.description: Defines force as a push or pull.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying force as a push or pull.

rubric.why: Inertia is the tendency to resist a change in a body's state.
rubric.description: Defines inertia as resistance to change in state of rest or motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body resists a change in its state of rest or motion.

modelAnswer: Force is a push or pull that can change or tend to change the state of rest or motion of a body.
Inertia is the property of a body by which it resists a change in its state of rest or motion.

items.followUp: State the principle of moments for a body in equilibrium and write its equation.

rubric.why: The law applies when the body is in rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the body is balanced or in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the equilibrium condition.

rubric.why: The law equates the total clockwise and anticlockwise moments about the same pivot or point.
rubric.description: States the equality of clockwise and anticlockwise moments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equality about a pivot or point.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a point is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.
Sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments.

items.followUp: Define power and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Work is done when a force causes displacement in its direction.
rubric.description: Defines work in terms of force causing displacement in its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that work is done when a force moves a body through a displacement in the force's direction.

rubric.why: Energy is defined as the capacity or ability to do work.
rubric.description: Defines energy as the capacity to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of energy.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force displaces a body in the direction of the force.
Energy is the capacity to do work.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and write its equation.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with position or configuration.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy possessed due to position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking potential energy to a body's position or configuration.

rubric.why: This is the equation for gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface.
rubric.description: Writes the equation for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for PE = mgh, with equivalent notation accepted.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.

items.followUp: What is electrical energy? Give two sources of it.

rubric.why: Chemical energy is energy stored in chemical substances and released in chemical reactions.
rubric.description: Defines chemical energy as energy stored in chemical substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as energy stored in substances or chemical bonds.

rubric.why: Food and fuels are examples of sources of chemical energy.
rubric.description: Gives two sources of chemical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming two valid sources, such as food and fuels.

modelAnswer: Chemical energy is the energy stored in chemical substances, which can be released during a chemical reaction.
Two sources of chemical energy are food and fuels.

items.followUp: Define pressure and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Stress is defined as force acting per unit area.
rubric.description: Defines stress as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of stress is the pascal, equivalent to N/m².
rubric.description: States the SI unit of stress.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Pa or N/m².

modelAnswer: Stress is the force acting per unit area of a body.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to N/m².

items.followUp: State Hooke’s law and write the relation between stress and strain.

rubric.why: Hooke’s law states that extension is directly proportional to applied force within the elastic limit.
rubric.description: States the proportionality between extension and applied force, including the elastic-limit condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct law and its elastic-limit condition.

rubric.why: F = kx expresses the proportional relation between force and extension.
rubric.description: Writes the equation for Hooke’s law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F = kx or an equivalent rearrangement.

modelAnswer: Within the elastic limit, the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the applied force.
F = kx, where F is the applied force, x is the extension and k is the spring constant.
